title: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, and Evidence Workflows
author: Jordan Kim
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance standards for role-based access control (RBAC) and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC practices, incident response (security-focused), compliance evidence workflows, and the process for risk and exceptions. It is an operational reference for engineering, security, and compliance teams responsible for controls, evidence collection, and incident handling.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood-managed control plane services (redwood-auth, rbac-service, audit-log-collector, controlplane-api) and to Private/On-Prem deployments where customer-managed networks are in use.
- Covers production and sensitive staging environments; developer sandbox environments are subject to a reduced set of controls (see Appendix).

Ownership and Contacts

- Control owner: Security (security@redwood.com)
- Primary maintainers: Identity Platform (team: identity-platform) and Observability (team: observability)
- Escalation: On-call Security Incident Response (pager: #sec-incident)

Key Principles

1. Least privilege by default - deny unless explicitly allowed.
2. Strong, auditable authentication with short-lived credentials where possible.
3. Immutable evidence and tamper-evident audit logs retained to meet compliance windows.
4. Secure SDLC with gated code review and signed releases for runtime components.
5. Clear exception and risk acceptance workflows with owner and review cadence.

RBAC & Authentication

Goals:
- Ensure access is role-based, least privilege, and centrally managed.
- Provide automated provisioning (SCIM) for enterprise customers and SSO integrations.

Standards:
- Identity provider (IdP): Okta (primary); Azure AD (secondary for customers using dedicated integrations).
- Service accounts: Managed in identity-platform, labeled with prefix svc/ and assigned least privileges.
- Roles: Use canonical role set: viewer, developer, operator, maintainer, security-admin, infra-admin. Custom roles require security review.
- Policy storage: Role definitions and policy bindings are stored in git (repo: infra/iam-policies) and deployed through identity-platform CI.

SLOs and Thresholds:
- Authentication API latency: 99th percentile < 100ms for controlplane-api in US regions.
- Provisioning consistency: SCIM group-sync success rate >= 99.9% per 24h window.
- Privilege escalation detection: Any change to security-admin bindings must trigger an audit webhook and a notification to #security-alerts.

Operational Procedures (examples):
1) New role creation
   - Author submits ADR in infra/iam-policies with rationale and owner.
   - Security performs a review within 3 business days.
   - Changes merged to infra/iam-policies and deployed via identity-platform CI.
2) Emergency access (break-glass)
   - Request through the break-glass form (internal link) with approval from Security Director.
   - All break-glass sessions are time-limited (max 4 hours) and logged at audit-level HIGH.

Audit Logging

Goals:
- Capture authentication, authorization decisions, administrative actions, configuration changes, and data access events.
- Ensure logs are immutable, searchable, and retained per policy.

Architecture:
- Producers: controlplane-api, rbac-service, redwood-auth, model-serving-proxy, data-storage-gateway.
- Collector: audit-log-collector (runs in high-availability mode); forwards to internal S3-backed archive and to Splunk for day-to-day search.
- Immutability: Archive bucket has object-lock enabled (governance-mode) for retention windows.

Minimum Log Schema (required fields):
- timestamp, service, event_type, principal_id, principal_type, resource, action, outcome, request_id, trace_id, ip_address, user_agent.

Retention & SLOs:
- Production security logs: 7 years archival retention (compliance).
- Hot-search retention (Splunk / 90d index): 90 days.
- Log delivery SLA: 99.5% of events delivered to archive within 5 minutes.

Alerting & Monitoring:
- Missing-log detection: If the rate of expected events drops by > 30% for 10 minutes, fire PagerDuty to Observability and Security.
- Integrity check: Weekly hash verification between Splunk index and S3 archive; discrepancies >0.1% trigger investigation.

Data Residency & Retention

Residency Controls:
- Region tags: All customers and resources are tagged with residency-region (example: eu-west-1, us-east-1, ap-southeast-1).
- Data plane placement: For hosted customers with EU-only residency, all persistent data (embeddings, audits, logs) must remain in eu-west-1 buckets and compute in eu-west-1 zones.
- Cross-region replication: Disabled by default for residency-restricted customers; explicit approval from Legal + Security required.

Retention Policy (default):
- Audit logs (security events): 7 years archived, 90 days hot.
- Usage telemetry (non-identifiable): 2 years archived.
- Customer content (per plan): Hosted default 30 days; enterprise customers may contract different windows (configurable at provisioning).

Retention Procedure:
1. Retention configuration is stored in infra/retention-config.yaml and deployed by infra CI.
2. A monthly job (retention-enforcer) reconciles bucket object lifecycles vs policy and generates a report to Compliance.
3. Deletion is soft by default (object move to quarantine/<date>) for 30 days before permanent deletion; quarantine access is restricted to Security+Legal.

Secure SDLC

Requirements:
- All code touching auth, RBAC, or audit paths requires:
  - Mandatory code review by two engineers including at least one with security-owner label.
  - Static analysis (SAST) and dependency scan passing in CI.
  - Secrets scan: No credentials in code; any detected secret triggers blocker.
  - Signed releases for runtime artifacts (GPG or sigstore).

Gated steps:
- Pre-merge: Lint, unit tests, SAST, dependency checks.
- Pre-release: Integration tests (including auth regression tests), threat-model review for significant changes, release notes with risk assessment.

Third-party & Dependency Risk Management:
- Critical dependencies (CVE severity >= 9.0 or exploit in the wild) must be remediated within 48 hours or have a documented compensating control.
- Dependency inventory maintained in deps/inventory.csv and reviewed weekly by Security.

Incident Response (Security)

Objectives:
- Contain incidents affecting authentication, authorization, and audit integrity.
- Preserve evidence and follow legal/compliance obligations for notification.

Classification:
- Sev1 Security Incident: Compromise of identity provider, active privilege escalation, deletion/tampering of audit logs, or confirmed exfiltration of customer data.
- Sev2: Suspicious auth events, repeated failed privilege elevation attempts, misconfiguration affecting residency.

Runbook (high level):
1) Detection
   - Alert from monitoring (example: sudden admin role binding change or audit-log-collector failure).
2) Triage
   - Security on-call creates an incident in the incident tracker (prefix SEC-).
   - Capture initial snapshot: list of affected principals, recent role changes, relevant log extracts.
3) Containment
   - Rotate compromised credentials, revoke sessions for affected principals, disable implicated service tokens.
   - If audit-store may be compromised, isolate archive bucket and snapshot current state.
4) Evidence preservation
   - Export relevant logs (store in evidence-bucket with object-lock).
   - Generate signed manifests of evidence captured and hand off to Legal if required.
5) Remediation & Recovery
   - Apply patches, roll back misconfigurations, re-run infra compliance scans.
6) Post-incident
   - 72-hour incident summary posted to /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems and a formal Incident Review within 10 business days.

Notifications and Legal
- For incidents impacting customer data or residency guarantees, Security notifies Legal within 2 hours of classification.
- Regulatory notifications (e.g., GDPR) follow legal guidance and are tracked in the incident record.

Compliance Evidence Workflows

Purpose:
- Define how control evidence is collected, validated, and stored to support audits (SOC2, ISO27001, regional privacy assessments).

Evidence Types & Owners:
- RBAC policy definitions: Owner: Identity Platform (evidence: infra/iam-policies git history + deployment logs).
- Audit log retention proof: Owner: Observability (evidence: S3 object-lock manifests, Splunk retention config).
- Secure SDLC attestations: Owner: Eng DevEx (evidence: CI run artifacts, signed releases, review logs).

Workflow:
1) Evidence Collection
   - Controls are mapped in the controlbook; each control links to required artifacts and owners.
   - Automated collectors (evidence-bot) snapshot git SHAs, CI run IDs, and log manifests weekly.
2) Validation
   - Compliance Run: Monthly, Compliance team runs automated checks vs expected artifacts; manual checks quarterly.
3) Storage
   - All evidence stored in evidence-archive (S3, restricted) with metadata CSV (evidence-index.csv).
4) Audit Response
   - For auditor requests, create a scoped evidence package with signed manifests and chain-of-custody notes.

Risk & Exceptions

Process:
- Exceptions to the standards above require a documented Risk Exception request with: owner, compensating controls, duration (max 90 days), and risk acceptance signature from Security and the relevant service owner.
- All exceptions are tracked in the Risk Exceptions Register (spreadsheets: compliance/risk-exceptions.csv) and reviewed monthly by Security and Legal.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Compensating controls must provide equivalent security posture (e.g., additional monitoring, reduced blast radius, enhanced logging).
- Temporary exceptions require a remediation plan and a calendar task assigned to the service owner.

Example: Temporary cross-region replication enabling for backup purposes
- Request: infra-team requests enabling replication for region us-west-2 -> us-east-1 for a 30-day migration window.
- Compensating controls: encryption-in-transit with forced TLS 1.3, object-level encryption, restricted replication IAM role, audit-log forwarder verifying replication events.
- Approval: Security + Legal sign; exception recorded with 30-day expiry and automatic revoke job.

Appendix

1) Example log entry (JSON line)
{"timestamp":"2027-12-01T15:04:05Z","service":"rbac-service","event_type":"role_binding.change","principal_id":"u:12345","resource":"project:prod-123","action":"add","outcome":"success","request_id":"req-abc-123","trace_id":"trace-xyz","ip_address":"34.55.66.77"}

2) Retention configuration example (infra/retention-config.yaml)
- audit_logs:
    archive_retention_days: 2555  # 7 years
    hot_retention_days: 90
- customer_content_default_days: 30

3) Useful CLI snippets
- To export a policy binding history: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://controlplane-api.internal/v1/iam/policies?resource=project:prod-123&history=1" > policy-history.json
- To snapshot audit logs for evidence: aws s3 cp s3://audit-archive/prod/2027-12-01 evidence/ --recursive --profile evidence-reader

4) Related controls and pages
- infra/iam-policies (git)
- controlbook: /confluence/security-and-compliance/security-and-compliance-controlbook-2026-03-04
- Incident playbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process
